4284ca6cec1e20fd: PETALING JAYA, Sep 13 — In this line of work, I get all sorts of tips in all shapes and sizes.

Over drinks with a friend. Chatting with my aunt(ies). Being sent a zoomed-in screenshot of my friend’s colleague’s boyfriend’s sister’s Instagram story — you know, the sort of boots-on-the-ground journalism we’ve come to expect in our time.
In a first, I was tipped off to a char kuey teow stall after my parents tried it at a birthday party.

It was a grand affair — the sort with themed costumes and bespoke invitations, it was a 50th birthday after all — but the food remained firmly on the ground; char kuey teow just happened to be one of the birthday boy’s favourites.

The stall, Pei Yin Char Kuey Teow, booked by the birthday boy himself, turned out to be much closer to home than expected: 111 Beet Fatt Restaurant, Damansara Utama, also home to the fairly popular SBay Wantan Mee.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
111 Bee Fatt Restaurant spans two shops in Damansara Utama along the row facing the Uptown 5 office towers.

I first tried it for myself about a month ago, ordering a “small” (RM10) portion. I was struck by the fat, firm prawns; the balance of savouriness and wok hei; and, quite stealthily, the intensity of spice.
When I ordered, the friendly assistant asked if I wanted laat jiu, which I confirmed without thinking much of it. It didn’t overwhelm the rest of the plate, but it certainly didn’t go unnoticed.
If you like your char kuey teow with a kick, this one’s for you.

I went back again recently, trying two different modifications: extra cockles (RM4) and a fried egg (RM1). I’m not the biggest fan of cockles, but I do appreciate that when they mean extra cockles, they mean it.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Pei Yin is located on the right side of the shop, in the section that opens out into the paved alleyway.
Plump, blood-red and briny, they covered half the plate, delivering anyone looking for that iron-rich, metallic hit exactly what they came for.
The game changer for me was the fried egg — I love a fried egg and a runny yolk, and I can’t believe it’s taken me this long to add one to my char kuey teow order.
My only gripe: I wish the edges were crispier, but the yolk was perfect, runny and slipping oozily between strands of charred kuey teow.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
A perfectly runny yolk in a fried egg is the cherry on top of the icing on a plate of satisfying ‘char kuey teow’.
If you’re looking to plan a visit, early morning is your best bet. Pei Yin starts the day at six in the morning, but even at eight, it’s still relatively easy to get in and out.
And if you’re looking to cater your next party — treating your guests to a very satisfying plate of char kuey teow — Pei Yin caters within the Klang Valley, with a minimum order of 100 plates.
A hundred plates might sound like a big ask, but if you ever need help eating through them, I’m your man.
Pei Yin Char Kuey Teow,
111 Bee Fatt Restaurant
26, Jalan SS 21/39,
Damansara Utama, Petaling Jaya.
Open Monday to Saturday, 6am-2pm

8d2be15be7126a2d: KUANTAN, Sept 13 — An Indian national drowned after she was believed to have slipped off a boat following a scuba diving activity in the waters of Renggis, Pulau Tioman in Rompin yesterday.
Rompin district police chief Supt Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said police received a call from the Tekek Health Clinic at about 10 am regarding the drowning of Sabiya Shiek, 65.
He said initial investigations revealed the victim had taken part in a discovery scuba diving session with six family members, accompanied by two instructors and a dive master.
“After the session, the victim informed the instructor that she wished to return to the boat.
“However, after her child helped remove her diving gear, Sabiya is believed to have slipped while climbing the ladder to get on board and fell back into the sea,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He said diving instructors launched an immediate search and located the victim about 15 minutes later, lying unconscious on the sandy seabed near the dive site.

The victim was taken to the Tekek Health Clinic on Pulau Tioman, where a medical officer pronounced her dead, with a post-mortem scheduled at the Tengku Ampuan Afzan Hospital here on Monday. — Bernama
0897a81d5cf94b96: BALTIMORE, (Maryland): South Africa felt their tour series against New Zealand was in the balance up until the final 10 minutes of the last test, before they went on to register a 43-28 win and secure the trophy 3-1.
Coach Rassie Erasmus said he was not confident of victory until the last stages of the final clash, staged in the United States on Saturday.

New Zealand had won the opening test in Johannesburg last month in a blistering start to the six-week tour, but the world champion Springboks bounced back to win the next two games and make sure they could not lose the series.
But an All Blacks victory in Baltimore would have made it 2-2 and seen the spoils shared, and New Zealand fought back strongly in the second half.

"In minute 70, I thought it was still in the balance. In the end, we came out winners because we had more points on the board, and that's probably the most important thing," he told the post-match press conference.

"Although you have different things that you're trying to do, build your game, get your attacks going, and defend better, but it's all about the scoreboard, and up until the last 10 minutes, I wasn't sure we were going to win."

South Africa had a narrow 17-14 lead at halftime but stretched that with two quick tries in the second half, only for New Zealand to fight back and reduce the deficit to eight points before a superb individual try by Bok winger Kurt-Lee Arendse allowed them breathing space.
"We appreciate that we won, but we definitely don't think the margin between us and New Zealand is big," Erasmus added.
The South African camp praised the support received from the 68,000-strong crowd.

The decision to take the last test of "Rugby's Greatest Rivalry" to the US was designed to fill the coffers of the two unions who share the profits of the tour, the first of its kind in 30 years and now scheduled to be played every four years.
"It was super special. It was crazy the amount of people who came out to support us," said Springbok captain Siya Kolisi.
"We're hoping that the game grows here, because we know that the (2031) World Cup is going to be here," he added. — REUTERS
617a3ddbc8dd9fea: LIVERPOOL: Andoni Iraola said it was obvious Liverpool suffered from fatigue in a 0-0 draw at home to Fulham on Saturday, but insisted his players have to adapt to a gruelling schedule.

Less than three days on from beating Atletico Madrid 2-1 in their Champions League opener, the Reds were comfortably held at bay by a Fulham side that had lost each of their first three Premier League games under Alvaro Arbeloa.
"Our players were tired," said Iraola. "We cannot hide it. I think it's the worst turnaround in terms of 60 something hours between the games, after a very big game the other day.
"This is going to happen more times, maybe with one more day, but sometimes it's going to happen the same way during the season. We have to adapt to these circumstances.

"It's these kinds of games that you need to win; sometimes with a set play, sometimes with a shot from the edge (of the box), sometimes from a moment of brilliance from the offensive players. We haven't had that today."
Bradley Barcola failed to shine on his full Premier League debut on an off day for Liverpool's near £500 million forward line also featuring Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Victor Munoz.
Iraola remains unbeaten since taking charge of the 20-time English champions, but three of his first four Premier League games have now ended in disappointing draws.
"It's the first game since I'm here I think we've had problems to create chances, to score goals, to make the difference offensively," added Iraola.
"That's the main reason that we couldn't create as many chances as we wanted."--AFP
3aa6444ffe652474: OTA BHARU, Sept 13 — A 23-year-old Thai man was found drowned in Sungai Golok along the Malaysia-Thailand border near Kampung Pengkalan Pasir and Abe Yie in Rantau Panjang, Pasir Mas yesterday evening.

659dcd07d8abd7ea: KUALA LUMPUR: On paper, the Olympic Council of Malaysia has charted a cautious course for the national sailing squad at the Asian Games, setting a target of one silver and five bronze medals.

But out on the water, team manager Afendy Abdullah believes the winds of fortune in Aichi-Nagoya could carry not only Malaysia's seasoned champions to the top step, but also propel a crop of young talents into medal contention.
"If everything we have planned falls into place and the elements align with our preparations, that gold medal will be there," Afendy told Timesport.

"In sailing, we do not face a direct human antagonist on the pitch… we are racing against the weather, tides and changing sea conditions. If the wind matches what we have prepared for, we can match anyone."
Afendy, however, refuses to romanticise the challenge and admits there is a clear disparity in international exposure between Malaysia and Asia's sailing powerhouses.

"Other nations competed in seven or eight overseas regattas, we only managed two. Naturally, those who gained more exposure hold the edge. But all we can do now is maximise our preparation and make every race count," he said.
Malaysia have enjoyed a strong Asian Games sailing pedigree since Ryan Tan captured the men's Optimist gold at Hiroshima 1994.

The roll of honour includes Doha 2006, where Rufina Tan became Malaysia's first female Asian Games sailing gold medallist in the Optimist, while Nurul Elia Anuar claimed Laser 4.7 bronze at Incheon 2014.

Faizal Norizan-Syukri Aziz later struck 420 gold, while sailors including Nazmi Sharif, Malik Sulaiman, Latif Khan, Ku Anas Ku Kamil-Hafizuddin Mazelan, Khairunnisa Afendy-Norashikin Sayed, Nuraisyah Jamil, Umi Norwahida Sallahuddin and Ilham Wahab-Nur Fatin Solehah also recorded podium finishes across several editions.
The men's Laser has contributed silver medals through two eras - Kevin Lim in 1998 and 2002, and Khairulnizam Afendy in 2014 and 2018 - although gold has remained elusive.
The traditional Laser category, however, will not be contested in Aichi-Nagoya, with the programme featuring selected dinghy and skiff events.
The 12-member squad includes three returning medallists who have won five Asian Games medals between them, including two champions.
The spearhead is defending champion Nur Shazrin Latif, who has one gold and one bronze after becoming Malaysia's first female sailor to win the Laser Radial/ILCA 6 title at Hangzhou 2022.
Shazrin is already in Gamagori, Aichi, acclimatising alongside the 29er crew.
The veteran core is strengthened by four-time Olympian Khairulnizam, the most experienced returning male medallist.
After finishing eighth in Hangzhou, he heads into the Games free from the injury problems that hampered his previous campaigns.
"Over the last six years, Khairulnizam was constantly under intense pressure while battling through surgeries and a slipped disc," said Afendy.
"Today, he is in a far better place physically and emotionally. He is fully prepared to mount a serious challenge."
Joining him is 2018 men's Laser 4.7 gold medallist Fauzi Kaman Shah, who Afendy believes has developed the tactical discipline and maturity needed for senior-level racing.

The squad comprises six men and six women, with nine debutants, including Iqbal Nazham Musmuliadi, Adam Aierell Azizol Amirul, Aiman Aqeel Firdaus, Danyal Marczqui Rahmat Haron Muzaffar, Nur Hafizanah Zailan, Juni Karimah Noor Jamali, Nor Izniey Humaira Azri, Aina Zulaikha Azizul Rahman and Nur Aina Norhazram.
Afendy believes the newcomers can compete with Asia's best.
"In the Under-17 and Under-19 categories, our rivals do not have a 10-year head start because sailors switch boat classes at roughly the same age.
"The playing field is level. Whoever possesses mental grit and sharp execution will have a genuine shot at a breakthrough."

f0d8920040712859: LONDON: Xabi Alonso admitted he would love Chelsea to give him a "boring game" after their defensive woes allowed Hull to escape Stamford Bridge with a 2-2 draw on Saturday.
Alonso's side were cruising after Morgan Rogers drilled home in the seventh minute, but once again they paid the price for some sloppy defending.
Hull's Algerian winger Mohamed Belloumi blasted the equaliser after Chelsea failed to clear a long ball.
And Belloumi put the tireless Tigers in front when his deflected shot flashed in before half-time.
Cole Palmer's incisive run and cut-back in the 66th minute allowed Joao Pedro to bag Chelsea's equaliser.
But the Blues were unable to find a winner and have now conceded nine goals in their four Premier League matches this season.
They also shipped three goals against Leeds in midweek but ran out 6-3 winners in the League Cup third round tie.
That chaotic clash encapsulated Chelsea under Alonso, who was hired in the close season to improve their fortunes after last term's disappointing 10th place finish.
The Spaniard is well aware that Chelsea's attacking quality, which has brought 10 goals in four league games, is being dented by their issues in defence.
"Maybe entertaining, but I hope one day you'll say it was a boring game and we win and we don't give these entertaining moments," Alonso said.
"It kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to fix them.
"When we get the lead, you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially for the first goal. We can do much better. It was too soft.
"That momentum that we had (was lost), it changed the mood. It's something we need to keep talking (about) and address. We will get better, but it's having an impact on our performances."
Chelsea have been highly entertaining in the season's early weeks but their inability to control matches has become a concern.
Hull could have been out of sight had Emiliano Martinez not recovered from a fumble to clear the danger as Oli McBurnie looked poised to make it 3-1.
"Overall I think that we are attacking better than defending," said Alonso.
"It's a big topic and a big theme for us. It's just four games, but the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don't like it.
"We can do better for sure. When we have the lead, a very important part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distances. I'm sure that we can do better."
Hull have made a superb start after their unexpected promotion last season via the Championship play-offs.
Tigers boss Sergej Jakirovic, whose third-placed team are still unbeaten, said: "I feel good. We have to be happy. It's a huge result for us.
"We had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie, but Martinez's save was excellent.
"We can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd
a83f92a23a62dcb2: ISTANBUL, Sept 13 — Accounts of more than a dozen Turkish LGBTQ organisations have been blocked on the X social media platform at the request of authorities advocating traditional family values, a watchdog said on Saturday.
Among the blocked accounts are that of Kaos GL rights organisation and lawyer Levent Piskin, the Ifod media watchdog said.
The X accounts, followed by tens of thousands of people, were not accessible in Turkey without a VPN connection, AFP observed on Saturday.
Turkey’s LGBTQ community has been frequently targeted by the authorities, with President Recep Tayyip Erdogan lashing the community as a “deviant movement” of “perverts”.
In June, Turkey blocked some 40 X accounts linked to feminist or LGBTQ groups.

Last year, the Turkish authorities persuaded X to block more than 700 accounts critical of authorities, at the height of a wave of protests triggered by the arrest of Istanbul’s opposition mayor, Ekrem Imamoglu. — AFP
3d82ec23ab304a8f: LONDON: Roberto De Zerbi said sorry to Tottenham's furious fans after his winless side were booed off following their 0-0 draw against Everton on Saturday.
De Zerbi's side have yet to score a single goal in four Premier League matches this season and Tottenham supporters showed their frustration at the final whistle.
After the jeers had rained down from the stands, Tottenham boss De Zerbi said he understood the abuse.
"I'm sorry for the fans. They were fantastic today. It is normal, the reaction of the fans," he said.

Asked how he felt about the bleak start to the season after Tottenham splashed out more than £300 million (US$406 million) on 10 signings, De Zerbi said: "It is not a tough moment. A tough moment was last season in Sunderland when we were close to relegation.
"Now is one of the moments in football when you are rebuilding a team.
"We played very well in the first 30 minutes then we lost energy because our physical condition is not the best. We are working for that."
Tottenham's miserable form has left them languishing just above the relegation zone after two draws and two defeats from their first four games.
Their only win and goals this season came in a League Cup victory over second tier Charlton.
Tottenham's lack of attacking firepower is a major concern and De Zerbi conceded they lacked composure in the Everton penalty area.
"We didn't shoot enough for the quality of the play we showed. We had to shoot more times. We went inside the area 74 times but we didn't create enough for the quality of the play," he said.
"We have to work for sure. We have to analyse the quality of the decisions but we made too many wrong decisions. I'm not positive and I'm not negative. I am realistic.
"I have to analyse the performance and the potential situations when we could shoot and score with better decisions."
Tottenham only avoided relegation on the final day of last season and have finished 17th for the last two years.
Their summer spending spree was supposed to end their miserable period of underachievement.
But De Zerbi admitted his team lacked confidence as the game wore on, with the tense atmosphere in the stadium adding to their anxious display.
"I observed my players with a little less confidence in the second half and I don't like this. They need to understand that we are in the right way," he said.
"They are human. They are sensitive, they have emotions. My position is to help them and stay focused on the improvement we need to do.
"If we play 90 minutes like we did the first 30 we will win many games."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

16b25ef7f3d36a41: NEW DELHI, Sept 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said his meetings with representatives of several leading companies here today reflect the continued confidence of industry players and investors in Malaysia’s economic potential and direction.
“The Madani Government will continue to facilitate quality investments that strengthen local industries, create high-value jobs, and ensure that the benefits are felt by the people,” he said.

Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, met representatives of DRB-Hicom, Segula Technologies India, AWL Agri Business Ltd and Motherson Group to discuss opportunities to expand investment and industrial cooperation between Malaysia and India in strategic sectors.
The first meeting was held with representatives of DRB-Hicom, who were accompanied by their strategic partners, to explore opportunities for cooperation with the automotive industry in India.

“I then met with the leadership of Segula Technologies India, a global engineering and technology company, which expressed the intention to establish a global engineering centre in Malaysia by the end of 2026,” he said in a post on social media.

The initiative, he said, could strengthen Malaysia’s local engineering capabilities through the hiring of Malaysian talent and the application of artificial intelligence expertise in the automotive, aerospace, energy and advanced manufacturing sectors.

Meanwhile, the meeting with AWL Agri Business Ltd, one of the major companies in India’s agribusiness sector, explored efforts to increase its purchase of products from Malaysian suppliers, Anwar said.

The company has imported about RM1.5 billion worth of Malaysian palm oil products, creating opportunities to expand cooperation in palm oil, specialty fats, oleochemicals and other downstream products.
“I also met with representatives of Motherson Group, who shared plans to expand their information technology and digital solutions business in Malaysia,” the Prime Minister said.
The move would leverage on the strengths of local talent, Malaysia’s digital infrastructure, and the country’s strategic position as a gateway to regional markets, he added.
Anwar arrived here on Friday to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit. This is his second visit to India in his capacity as Prime Minister, following his visit in August 2024. — Bernama
8ba368e3a2f1c9aa: NEW DELHI, Sept 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to deliver a National Statement on Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth at the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit here today.

He is expected to emphasise the importance of strengthening cooperation among Brics member and partner countries in addressing development challenges, expanding economic opportunities and ensuring that the benefits of technological advancement and innovation are enjoyed more inclusively by all countries.
Malaysia’s participation in the summit is in its capacity as a Brics partner country, a status held since Jan 1, 2025.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, was accompanied by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri Ramanan Ramakrishnan.
The Prime Minister will also join in for a family photo with Brics leaders, partners and outreach invitees before heading to Kozhikode (Calicut), Keralam for the second leg of his visit in India.
In Keralam, he will meet with the Grand Mufti of India, Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad, to exchange perspectives on community development, educational advancement, and interfaith harmony.
As part of the visit, the Prime Minister is scheduled to meet Chief Minister Thiru V. D. Satheesan and Governor of Keralam Thiru Rajendra Vishwanath Arleka.
The engagements aim to strengthen bilateral cooperation between Malaysia and the state of Keralam across key sectors such as trade and investment, tourism, healthcare and education.
On Sept 14, Anwar will head to the Maldives. — Bernama
3bdea009b6d51cd8: SUNDERLAND: Mikel Arteta said the decision to award Sunderland a penalty could have cost Arsenal the Premier League title, even though his side emerged 2-0 winners at the Stadium of Light on Saturday.
Sunderland had the chance to take the lead early in the second period when Ezri Konsa was penalised for wrestling Dan Ballard to the floor.
Arteta was furious as pictures showed Ballard was also pulling the England international as the pair fell to the ground inside the Arsenal box.
The decision ultimately mattered little as Enzo Le Fee's spot-kick was brilliantly saved by David Raya.
Just two minutes later Bruno Guimaraes blasted Arsenal in front with his first goal for the club before Bukayo Saka's penalty sealed all three points in stoppage time.
But the result did not hold back Arteta's ire towards the officials.

"We have to go through what was done today that in my opinion is not acceptable. I watched it 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how they think to give a penalty in that situation or the way the VAR has not intervened," said Arteta.

"I don't know what to think really. I'm sad that we have to discuss in such a beautiful game something at this level that has the gravity of that because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship.
"At this level, with all the work that we put in, this cannot happen."

Guimaraes was Arsenal's big-money recruit of the transfer window, but the £75 million (US$87 million) signing is yet to start for his new club as Arteta has kept faith with Myles Lewis-Skelly alongside Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard in midfield.
The Brazilian was introduced at half-time and proved his worth with a brilliant strike to break the deadlock and silence the Sunderland fans that took aim at the former Newcastle captain.
Guimaraes also had a hand in Arsenal's second goal as from his pass, Saka was chopped down for the penalty.
"The personality that he has. He comes in and this is a special game for him as well, what it means for him, and how he grabs the game," added Arteta.
"The decisions that he's made and the two actions. The goal is incredible and the assist as well to Bukayo to put him through in front of goal, it's unbelievable as well."
A fourth win from four Premier League games takes the defending champions three points clear at the top of the table.--AFP
5e1accdc07a0485a: SYDNEY: One person died and 30 are missing after a ferry sank off the coast of Vanuatu, the South Pacific nation's government said on Sunday.
The vessel, MV Matui, had set sail on Friday with more than 40 passengers and crew from the island of Santo to Ambae island in very rough seas, but did not arrive.
"Our hearts and prayers are with the families who have lost loved ones. Search and rescue operations are continuing," read a statement from Vanuatu Prime Minister Jotham Napat's office on Sunday.
Fifteen of those onboard have been "accounted for alive" and one dead body has been recovered, the statement said.
"Over 30 people remain missing at sea," it said.
An investigation into potential negligence has been launched.
"This loss appears to be the result of strong winds and marine warnings not being heeded, and possibly of negligence including overloading of the vessel," the statement added.
The Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre in Noumea, New Caledonia said it is assisting with the search, and a French Armed Forces aircraft was deployed on Sunday morning.
The centre said 12 people were located on Sunday morning.
The member of parliament for Luganville, Matai Seremaiah, who is assisting in the search, said efforts would concentrate on the southeast coast where currents may have carried survivors. — AFP
a57b44219f12825a: PETALING JAYA: Umno Youth chief Dr Akmal Saleh’s claim that working with PAS is more consistent with the party’s principles may backfire if Umno fails to explain its continued participation in the unity government, says a political analyst.

While Akmal had every right to criticise the government, he lacked credibility in using “Umno’s principles” as the basis for rejecting Pakatan Harapan and DAP, said Ahmad Zaharuddin Sani Ahmad Sabri of Global Asia Consulting.
“If Umno’s principle is that it cannot work with DAP, why is Umno still in the federal government, where DAP is one of the component parties?” he told FMT.

On Thursday, Akmal said at the Umno Youth general assembly that PH had repeatedly tested Umno’s principles, dignity and Malay-Muslim sensitivities, making cooperation with PAS the more suitable option. "When people ask why Umno moved towards (cooperation with) PAS, don’t ask Umno. Ask PH why they made Umno choose between power and principles," he said.

He said Umno-Barisan Nasional had been prepared to remain in the opposition after the 2022 general election resulted in a hung Parliament, but agreed to form the government with PH and other coalitions out of respect for the king’s wishes.
However, Azmi Hassan of Akademi Nusantara said Akmal viewed such cooperation as a political choice rather than purely a matter of loyalty to the Malay rulers.
Azmi said Akmal and Umno Youth were clearly presenting cooperation with PAS as a political option, even though the party’s Supreme Council and top leadership had yet to make a final decision.

He said Akmal’s narrative also sought to suggest that although Umno was part of the government, its hands were tied because major policies were driven by PH, which is chaired by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
Zaharuddin said this was where Akmal’s “principle" argument became complicated, as compromise in a coalition government did not necessarily mean abandoning one’s principles.
“A principle used only to measure your opponents is no longer a principle. It becomes a political weapon,” he said.

Akmal had previously taken a hard line against DAP in Melaka, including resigning as a state executive councillor to “fight DAP”, while accepting Umno’s decision to remain in the unity government at federal level.

Zaharuddin said this difference must be explained clearly if Umno wanted voters to accept its argument on principle. “What is the difference between Melaka and Putrajaya? If the answer is political strategy, then say so,” he said.

He said Akmal’s criticism of the rising cost of living had some basis, but Umno could not simply criticise measures to address the issue without offering alternative policies, especially as it is also part of the government.
e3119e252e5fae76: KULAI: For many children, the best part of making a pizza might be choosing the toppings. At one hands-on class in Kulai, however, they are encouraged to start much earlier - with the dough.

Children taking part in the sessions knead, shape and prepare their own pizzas before watching them bake in a wood-fired oven, giving them a chance to experience the whole process rather than simply decorating a ready-made base.
The idea came about after parents dining at Qulai Pizza began asking owner Shahril Aman, 49, whether their children could have a go themselves. "So, we gave them the opportunity,” he told Bernama.

Photos of the activity gradually led to more enquiries from other families and kindergartens, particularly during the school holidays, and the informal sessions eventually became a regular morning programme.

For Shahril, the appeal goes beyond keeping children entertained: he wants them to experience the effort that goes into making something, from preparing the dough to handling a pizza paddle and seeing the finished result come out of the oven.
“For a group of around 20 children, the activity takes about one and a half to two hours, while larger groups can take up to three hours or more,” he said.
Some children are initially nervous about approaching the wood-fired oven, but Shahril sees that hesitation as part of the lesson.
“We want to boost their confidence because, to them, making a pizza seems difficult. But when they manage to do it, they will think, ‘Oh, I can actually do it!’”
The children are closely supervised throughout, particularly near the oven, while parents, teachers and staff are encouraged to keep the atmosphere positive.
Shahril said simple encouragement can make a noticeable difference. Children who are initially afraid may become eager to try again once they realise they can manage the task safely.
The programme also welcomes children with special needs, including those with autism, Down syndrome and cerebral palsy.
Shahril’s wife, who has a background in special education, helps support the sessions, allowing activities to be adapted according to a child’s comfort level and abilities.

Beyond baking, the kampung setting offers other small learning opportunities. Children can see fruit trees and herbs around the premises and observe the firewood used to heat the oven, giving the experience a more tactile feel than a typical indoor class.

Shahril himself did not begin his career anywhere near a kitchen. He previously worked in corporate roles before changing direction during the Covid-19 pandemic and learning pizza-making largely through online videos and experimentation.
That background may be why he sees value in allowing children to try something unfamiliar, make mistakes and discover that a difficult-looking task can become manageable with guidance.
For the children, the reward at the end is simple enough: a pizza they made themselves, still warm from the oven, and the satisfaction of knowing they managed every step along the way.

f1eb48ca53026442: PETALING JAYA: Dakwaan Ketua Pemuda Umno, Dr Akmal Saleh, bahawa kerjasama dengan PAS lebih selari dengan prinsip parti mungkin memakan diri jika Umno gagal menjelaskan penglibatan berterusan dalam kerajaan perpaduan, menurut penganalisis politik.

9196bd18f626d1c3: SANAA: Houthi fighters on Sunday said they used drones and missiles to attack a military base in southern Saudi Arabia as renewed fighting with Yemen's government forces forced growing numbers of civilians to flee.

The attack at the southern Sharurah base targeted "weapons depots and command and control centres that are managing the aggression against our nation and people", Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree wrote on X.
The date of the operation was not specified. Clashes have increased this week between the Iran-allied Houthis and Yemeni government forces, which are backed by Riyadh.
On Saturday, the government forces said they had struck Houthi fighters in the Red Sea city of Mocha, and later attacked other Houthi positions in the southwestern part of the country.
"Air Force of the Armed Forces targeted positions and barracks of the terrorist Houthi group with three airstrikes" in the Taiz region, the Yemeni military said Sunday in a post on X.
US news site Axios also reported that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman twice called US President Donald Trump to request strikes on the Houthis last week, but that the request was rejected.

The ongoing clashes follow a week-long Houthi offensive that culminated in the group capturing the remainder of Yemen's Red Sea coast and several strategic islands, cementing their hold on the Bab al-Mandab Strait at the sea's southern entrance.

The waterway has become an important artery for Saudi Arabian oil exports after Iran largely cut off shipments through the Gulf with its blockade on the Strait of Hormuz at the start of the Middle East war.
The Houthis have recently declared their own maritime blockade of Riyadh's Red Sea ports.

The government news agency Saba reported on Saturday that Yemeni "forces destroyed vehicles and weapons and killed members of the Houthi terrorist militia" near the port of Mocha, and quoted a spokesman for the forces as saying they had also struck Houthi targets just outside the city.
The Houthis, meanwhile, said on Saturday evening that over the past 48 hours, "Saudi enemy aircraft conducted 129 airstrikes" on areas under their control.
- 'NOT EVEN A SHELTER' -
Yemen's civil war, which began in 2014 with the Houthi capture of the capital Sanaa, had been dormant since a ceasefire in 2022 but roared back to life in July.
Saudi Arabia first entered the war on the side of Yemen's internationally recognised government in 2015 and continues to support the Aden-based administration.
On Saturday night, Saudi authorities said a Houthi projectile fell in an area near the border, hours after issuing alerts warning of the risk of possible attacks.
The civil defence directorate said the incident resulted "in two injuries and material damage to a mosque, several buildings, and vehicles."
The Yemeni civil war has uprooted millions of people, and the latest fighting has led even more to flee their homes.
The fall of Mocha to the Houthis on Thursday drove many residents to Aden, where the internationally recognised government is based.
One of the displaced, Abdulali al-Rajihi, said the Houthis "told us: 'Leave, scatter, you have half an hour'."
"We fled wearing the clothes on our backs. And we took our children, as much as we could manage."
Saddam Ali escaped from Al-Waziyah with his 11 children and a few possessions crammed into a small pick-up truck. He said he hadn't found a single free house in the city, "not even a shelter."
The UN's migration agency said on Saturday that, since July, 76,000 people had fled the fighting, a figure that had quadrupled since last week.
About 1,400 people had fled to Djibouti, the country's minister of economy and finance Ilyas Moussa Dawaleh said on Saturday.
The renewed fighting in Yemen has killed more than 500 people, according to sources on both sides.
- 'FINE AND DANDY' -
Trump on Saturday acknowledged speaking to the de facto Saudi leader but said the Houthis had also "called us and they don't want to fight with us."
He did not elaborate on whether Washington would take any action, but told reporters that "everything's gonna work out fine and dandy" in the region.
In 2025, the United States conducted a seven-week bombing campaign against the Houthis in response to their repeated attacks on Red Sea shipping in support of Hamas in the Gaza war.
That ended with a negotiated ceasefire, though the Houthis kept up their missile and drone attacks targeting Israel.
More recently, the group has resumed attacks on ships in the Red Sea after declaring their maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia.
In Yemen's capital Sanaa, Houthi supporters celebrated the freeing of 210 prisoners held in areas that fell to the group and had spent up to eight years in jail.--AFP

026e6be0d0e7e89c: KUALA LUMPUR: City dwellers and diners have raised safety and accessibility concerns after Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) decided to allow restaurant operators to place tables and chairs on walkways.

d985e3a7605f5de2: NEW DELHI: When rescue dog Chloe is not tumbling across the grass on a farm outside India’s tech capital, she is learning to sniff human breath for signs of cancer, with a little help from artificial intelligence.
Fitted with a 3D-printed helmet and harness packed with sensors, Chloe is part of an experimental effort to use dogs’ extraordinary sense of smell to develop a non-invasive test for the disease.

Research suggests dogs can be trained to detect cancer and other illnesses, from Parkinson’s disease to Covid-19. With this in mind, Bengaluru-based startup Dognosis is using AI to analyse dogs’ brain activity, breathing and body language, turning their reactions to scent into data.
“In an hour, they can do thousands of sniffs,” co-founder Akash Kulgod, 26, told AFP. “Each sniff can evaluate a sample.”

Early detection can make a crucial difference to cancer survival, but many patients in India are diagnosed only after the disease has advanced. Dog-based screening could potentially offer a simple first layer of testing, helping identify people who may need further checks.

Chloe, a Labrador mix, is one of 15 dogs being trained by the startup and fitted with customised data-gathering equipment. “It’s like a doggy ‘Iron Man’ suit,” said Kulgod, who studied cognitive science at the University of California, Berkeley.
A promising study
Research suggests disease can alter chemicals released by the body, creating distinctive odours. Dogs have around 300 million scent receptors, compared with about five million in humans.
A recent Dognosis study involving more than 1,500 participants across six hospitals in Karnataka state was published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology.
Their testing method was straightforward: each patient breathes into a cotton mask for about 10 minutes, after which it is sealed and taken to the lab. Patients do not meet the dogs.
The company said the method achieved more than 90% accuracy across seven major types of cancer, and now plans to test it in real-world programmes.
Cancer specialists not involved in the project voiced cautious optimism.

“The study is promising, as an early signal,” said Santhosh Kumar Devadas, head of oncology at Ramaiah Memorial Hospital. “But they need to do the study with a much larger group before we make any definitive conclusions.”
Neelesh Reddy, a senior consultant oncologist at Manipal Hospitals, added that “only time will tell how this technology will be useful to the actual patients”.
A dog’s work-life balance
India has described cancer as a major public health concern, with an estimated one in nine of its 1.4 billion people likely to develop the disease.

Most of Dognosis’s dogs are beagles, alongside some Malinois and Shepherd mixes, but only the best candidates are selected. All have good "work-life balance", with work limited to around 30 to 45 minutes a day.
At a centre called “Sniffspace”, the dogs test human samples on platforms fitted with automatic feeders that dispense treats as rewards.
Co-founder Itamar Bitan, who spent four years in an Israeli special-forces canine unit, said the dogs are trained using “positive reinforcement” to detect a “specific funky smell”.
“Some of the dogs run directly to the feeder expecting rewards, some freeze, and some will scratch the sample with excitement,” the 28-year-old said.
“But as long as the machine that learns how the dogs react to the sample is very consistent, we don’t really mind.”
a97448503eecc21e: PETALING JAYA: Umno perlu menunjukkan ia memahami mengapa rakyat merampas kuasanya pada pilihan raya lalu sekiranya mahu dilihat sebagai 'kerajaan peneraju' selepas PRU16, di sebalik retorik 'kerajaan menanti' pada Perhimpunan Agung Umno kali ini.

3a9078f2a9629205: If we sit long enough at a neighbourhood mamak restaurant or walk through a housing area during a festive open house, we will almost certainly see a version of Malaysia that warms the heart.

We will see an unspoken, everyday grace — neighbours helping neighbours without checking identity cards, youths playing football across cultural lines, and ordinary people sharing a quiet, unbothered pluralism.
It is the unglamorous bedrock of national survival, the messy, beautiful space where we actually live — the middle ground.
Yet running parallel to this is a very different reality: political machineries and machinations designed to dismantle this exact peace.
Human beings are wonderfully complicated. We carry within us a crowded pantheon of loyalties—we are neighbours, workers, parents, children of a specific soil, and participants in a shared civic life.
But our race- and religion-based political systems have a perennial, lazy habit of trying to strip away all that overlapping complexity and force us down into a single, unyielding box.
Decades ago, the Lebanese-French essayist Amin Maalouf warned that humanity was perpetually trapped in a tribal reflex that reduced a person to a single, belligerent affiliation.
When identity is treated like a fortress rather than a bridge, politics stops being an art of negotiation and becomes an exercise in keeping people out.

The philosopher Amartya Sen called this the “miniaturisation” of human beings—the deliberate political push to shove individuals into a preordained tribal category while erasing everything else that they are.
We can watch this ancient script play out in real time in contemporary Malaysia, particularly through the majoritarian identity strategies championed by several parties.
The latest iteration of this was seen at the PAS muktamar on Sept 5, where a motion was passed to strengthen Malay Muslim political unity ahead of the next general election.

On paper, the rhetoric often sounds noble, coated in religious obligation and duty. And to be clear, there is nothing morally wrong or criminal in calling for Muslim unity — indeed, many in PAS and elsewhere frame it as a spiritual and communal duty.
Yet there is a profound historical irony. Islamic political ethics and classical scholarship have long warned against ‘asabiyyah’ — tribal fanaticism and blind group chauvinism.

Most of us know that political actors have a habit of masking their appeals in the universal language of faith and unity while weaponising group feeling to draw an invisible, suffocating circle around the nation.

To make a singular identity pitch work, political architects must manufacture a profound sense of paranoia. They must convince the group that they are under constant, existential threat, painting a picture of a civilisation right on the brink.

For instance, we have heard politicians from several parties — PAS, Umno, Bersatu, and even former prime minister Mahathir Mohamad — openly claim that Islam is under threat in Malaysia or that Malays are losing their land, their Tanah Melayu.
This manufactured fear crowds out rational, ethical concern — economic well-being, clean governance, and cross-cultural empathy — replacing it with the adrenaline of tribal survival.
The immediate casualty of this game is that fragile middle ground I mentioned above.

Exclusive identity politics — whether involving Malays, Chinese, Indians, Kadazandusuns or Muslims and non-Muslims — leaves zero room for moderation. Anyone who steps outside the tribal line or tries to build a bridge across communities may be branded a traitor to the cause.

It herds citizens into a zero-sum game, demanding that they view their neighbours — the very people who helped them shovel mud during floods or shared office space with them for years — not as fellow human beings, but as demographic adversaries.

Unity for an exclusive group always requires an “out-group” to define itself against. Calling for Muslim unity means drawing a circle to leave out the non-Muslims, just as calling for non-Muslim unity will draw a circle to leave out the Muslims.
Inside these invisible boundaries drawn by political players are those who fit the preferred mould; outside are millions of Malaysians who are instantly relegated to permanent political outsiders.

The long-term cost of this is deeply corrosive. A country cannot split its soul down demographic or religious lines without hollowing out its institutional backbone. When every ordinary civic issue is dragged into the tribal mud, compromise becomes impossible, and the state begins to fracture from within.

Malaysia sits today at a profound crossroads. On one side is the exhausting, vital work of defending the middle ground — the everyday commitment to a plural society where differences are respected rather than weaponised. On the other lies the comfortable, seductive trap of the single affiliation, where politicians harvest short-term wins by promising supremacy to one group at the expense of everyone else.

True political maturity takes the courage to step away from the politics of paranoia, protect our fragile middle ground, and heed the timeless warning: that a house built on the exclusion and subjugation of its own people can never truly stand.

As we celebrate the formation of Malaysia, we need to move away from the politics of identity to what I would call the politics of citizenship — where we are all citizens regardless of our racial origin or religion, and where Malaysian unity trumps all other unities.

2e35c2046e8a4695: PARIS: Celine Dion wept tears of joy on Saturday as she fulfilled her dream of returning to the stage after years battling a rare neurological disorder, with a sell-out concert in Paris.

The 58-year-old French Canadian singer appeared visibly moved as she opened her first full concert in six years with her 1990s French-language ballad "On ne change pas" ("One Doesn't Change"), singing to a crowd of 30,000 enthralled fans that one newspaper said included US former first lady Michelle Obama.
"These are, of course, tears of joy. I'm so delighted to see you," Dion said, blowing kisses to the audience at the packed Plenitude Arena on the western edge of Paris.

Her return to the stage underscored a remarkable comeback after Stiff Person Syndrome, an incurable condition that causes stiffness and cramps, forced her to cancel shows and cast years of uncertainty over whether she would ever perform again.
"The path was rockier than expected," she said, speaking in French and English.
"But I held on to a faint ray of light in the distance, deep in the mountains."
"Tonight, I want to sing for you, sing for myself, sing for life," she added.
'Unreal'
The largely female crowd sported sequined dresses and tops, glittered cheeks, and T-shirts emblazoned with the star's image or nods to her biggest hits.
"It's unreal to be here!," said Elisabeth Landry, a 38-year-old Quebecer who lives near the star's hometown of Charlemagne.
"I was convinced we'd never see her again, especially not embarking on a run of concerts like this."
French daily Le Parisien said the former first lady of the US was "discreetly attending this first concert".
Just hours before, one of the best-selling singers of all time greeted admirers outside her luxury hotel a short walk from the Arc de Triomphe.
Albertina Cabral, a fan from the Brazilian city of Sao Paulo, said she could barely put her feelings into words.
"It's unbelievable to stay here and to go to the concert and to see Celine so close," she said. "And she's feeling good, she's happy."
Paris spared no effort in welcoming Dion, drawing thousands of fans from across the world, including some who flew in from as far away as the French Polynesian island of Tahiti.
For days, Paris played host to costume contests, giant karaoke parties and tribute cruises on the Seine.

On Friday, the iconic cauldron rose above the Tuileries Garden, echoing the diva's surprise appearance up the Eiffel Tower to perform "Hymn to Love" by Edith Piaf during the opening ceremony of the Paris Olympics in 2024.
A lyric from the song, "I'd go and fetch the moon if you asked me to", along with the singer's first name, was projected in big letters onto the balloon.
The suburban train station serving the arena has been temporarily renamed "Celine."
'A legend'
Chloe and Katy Rydquist, who travelled from London, had spent around £1,500 on their tickets, saying Dion's return to the stage justified the cost.
"She's a legend," said Chloe.
The star's residency is projected to generate hundreds of millions of euros in economic benefits.
She kicks off her 26-date run with 16 sold-out shows in September and October, before returning for another 10 in May.
Fans who missed out on tickets have found other ways to catch a glimpse of their idol.
Dion has regularly stepped outside the Royal Monceau hotel to greet waiting fans, at times breaking into song and dance with them well into the early hours.
Over her four-decade career, Dion has sold around 260 million albums in English and French, with hits including "It's All Coming Back to Me Now" and "Because You Loved Me".
Dion revealed in late 2022 that she had been diagnosed with Stiff Person Syndrome, an autoimmune condition that can cause severe muscle stiffness and agonising spasms.
Dion has described it as making her feel as though she is being strangled, with cramps so intense they have left her with broken ribs.
She has returned to stage after what she has described as years of training "like an athlete", doing ballet and pilates several times a week, as well as voice therapy.
6bb497594be69079: KUALA LUMPUR: Restaurant operators have welcomed Kuala Lumpur City Hall's (DBKL) decision to allow eateries to place tables and chairs on five-foot walkways, but emphasised that member restaurants will strictly prioritise customer safety.
Malaysian Indian Restaurant Owners Association president Datuk J. Govindasamy said while operators are eager to start expanding, safety cannot be compromised.
"My advice to members is to apply properly, get the licence and above all, look out for customer safety," he told the New Sunday Times.
"Do not just pay the RM30 fee and put tables in unsafe spots, such as sharp road corners where vehicles turn. Safety must come first."
He said members are awaiting guidelines from DBKL before setting up any outdoor tables.
"I haven't been given any guidelines yet, but they mentioned we can use the outside space and that guidelines will be sent as soon as possible.
"Once the guidelines are out, we can apply to DBKL and start to operate."
Govindasamy said the initiative will benefit both business owners and local government revenue, provided it is managed safely.
"Most customers prefer sitting outside. It will increase our business while allowing the government to collect revenue through permit fees and taxes."
On concerns about walkways being blocked for pedestrians, wheelchair users and the visually impaired, he said outdoor seating should only be permitted where space allows.

"That is why we have to wait for the guidelines to see which areas DBKL permits. If a five-foot way is narrow, you cannot use it because it will block people. But some walkways are 10 to 12 feet wide, so DBKL will need to establish a proper scale for each location."
He added that they are representing over 200 Indian restaurant operators in Kuala Lumpur.
Malaysian Muslim Restaurant Owners Association Datuk Mohamed Mosin Abdul Razak said while the association supports the move, public accessibility and safety must remain paramount.
"For many restaurants, especially smaller Muslim-owned establishments, the five-foot way provides valuable additional dining space.
"Instead of having a situation where some operators use the space without clear approval while others face enforcement, a proper permit system gives businesses a legal and structured way to operate."
Mosin said pedestrian movement must not be compromised under the new scheme.

"Public access must remain the priority. We support outdoor dining only where there is sufficient space and where pedestrians, wheelchair users, senior citizens, parents with prams and emergency services are not inconvenienced."
While extra seating can boost revenue for smaller venues during peak hours, Mosin urged DBKL to provide clearer guidelines.
60441eb733b35051: NEW YORK: Elena Rybakina denied Aryna Sabalenka a third straight US Open title on Saturday, punctuating her rise to world number one with a 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 victory over the player she's replacing at the summit.

Kazakhstan's Rybakina, assured of supplanting Sabalenka atop the rankings by reaching the semi-finals in New York, won her third Grand Slam title to go with her 2022 Wimbledon crown and the Australian Open trophy she lifted this year with a win over Sabalenka.
Rybakina has played three of her four Grand Slam finals against Sabalenka, winning two and losing one, at the 2023 Australian Open.
"I can't find the words now," Rybakina said as she accepted the trophy at a tournament where she had never before made it past the fourth round. "I'm falling more and more in love with New York."
Sabalenka, unbeaten in 20 prior matches at Flushing Meadows, clawed back courageously in the second set, breaking Rybakina for the first time in the final game to force the third.
But with her trademark aplomb, Rybakina roared back to finish off a frustrated Sabalenka, who smashed her racket while sitting in her chair as her opponent was applauded by the crowd.
Sabalenka, 28, will end the year without a major title for the first time since 2022.

The two biggest hitters in the women's game came out swinging. After Rybakina held to love in the second game, she had Sabalenka in trouble in the third, unleashing a backhand passing winner to set up the first break chances of the match.

Sabalenka saved one break point with a forehand down the line and ripped another forehand winner on the next. A double fault gave Rybakina another look but Sabalenka held on with a volley winner before sealing the game with her first ace.

Two games later, however, Rybakina seized control as she relentlessly pushed Sabalenka back with her deep groundstrokes. Unsettled, Sabalenka double faulted on break point, then smacked a ball skyward to draw a code violation warning for ball abuse.
After another love hold from Rybakina, and a break point saved from Sabalenka, the margin was 4-3.
Rybakina hadn't committed a single unforced error through seven games and Sabalenka was looking increasingly desperate.
Serving to extend the set at 5-3, she crushed an overhead several feet beyond the baseline and had to regroup before closing the game with an ace and a service winner.

But Rybakina wouldn't be denied, and despite a hint of nerves as she coughed up her first double fault of the match, she polished off the set 6-4 with a screaming backhand winner before Sabalenka sailed a shot long to end the deciding rally.
- "I GUESS NEXT YEAR' -
The second set started much the same, Sabalenka saving a pair of break points in the third game before thumping down a massive serve to hold.
She had yet to make any headway against Rybakina's serve, but she seemed to have found something on her own, twice holding to love as she took a 5-4 lead.

Sabalenka's first break points of the match gave her a chance to close out the set, but she smacked a forehand long on the first and belted a service return long on the second as Rybakina leveled the set at 5-5.
Nevertheless, Sabalenka was gaining in confidence. She held for a 6-5 lead then broke Rybakina with authority to force a third set – but it proved only a brief reprieve.
"I wish I could have performed a little better," Sabalenka told the Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd, her voice breaking, "but I guess next year."--AFP
